jsonLd.name: Welcome to Calendly
jsonLd.transcript:
Hi there. Welcome to Calendly. Our research shows that it takes an average of seven emails back and forth to schedule one meeting. And then there are the no shows, the group meetings, the time zone math. Scheduling calls and meetings wastes a lot of time. That's why we created Calendly, a scheduling tool designed to make finding a time to meet easy and fast. Here's how it works.

First, you share your Calendly link with someone via email, text, LinkedIn, you name it. When they click your link, it'll look something like this. They'll choose a date and a time that works best for them. They'll enter some information and the calendar invite will be automatically emailed to both of you.

In seconds, a meeting is born. Now we know what you might be thinking. So I'm sharing my calendar with everyone and giving up complete control of my schedule? Quite the opposite.

Calendly puts you in complete control of your schedule. Here's how. First, you'll connect Calendly with the calendar you use every day with just a few clicks. Calendly will automatically reference that calendar and make sure your booking page accurately reflects your availability there.

Next, you'll fine tune your availability within Calendly itself. You can block off entire days, create automatic buffer time for yourself between meetings, set limits for how many meetings can be scheduled in a day and more. Basically, you decide when, where and how you want to meet. And on the client's end, they'll see all the possibilities that you've offered wrapped up in a polished professional scheduling experience.

Again, Calendly only shows the time slots that you've chosen to share, not your entire schedule. So give Calendly a try because scheduling doesn't have to be painful and manual.

Get rid of all the back and forth and simplify complex scheduling.

Welcome to a more efficient way to manage all of your meetings.

jsonLd.name: Group Scheduling: Calendly vs. Doodle Polls
jsonLd.transcript:
Let's talk group scheduling because we've all been there. You know, the gigantic email thread that goes on for days, maybe even weeks, with still no meeting in You can save yourself from all that chaos with a meeting poll that makes it easy to find a time that works for everyone. And here's the good news. Tools like Calendly and Doodle will help you set this up in no time.

In this video, we're comparing these two options so you can choose the tool that works best for you. Let's start with what Calendly and Doodle have in common. Both tools offer polls so groups can vote on the best time to meet. They both adjust for time zones automatically.

They both can show your availability and let people book time with you. They both sync with your calendar so you can prevent double bookings. They have mobile apps so you can schedule on the go. They let you collect payments when someone books time with you.

And yes, both have free versions so you can get started without taking out your credit card. And here are three key differences. Number one, no follow-up needed. Calendly takes group scheduling from start to finish.

Share a poll, collect votes, and once there's a winner, Calendly books the meeting and sends the invites. So you can just sit back and enjoy the show. Doodle will help you with the poll, but you're on your own when it comes to locking in the meeting. Number two, no ads ever.

Here's a little thing that can make a big impression. Calendly doesn't show ads, even on the free plan. So when guests book with you, it's clean, focused, and professional.

Doodle's free version does. It's not a deal breaker, just something to know. While both tools are easy to use, Calendly's end user experience is a bit cleaner, which makes it a favorite for folks who wanna look professional right from the start. Number three, more integrations.

Calendly plays nicely with tons of apps, Google Calendar, Zoom, Microsoft Teams, Outlook, Gmail, Salesforce, you name it. Doodle has the basics, calendar sync and some integrations. But if you're looking to connect a lot of tools automatically, Calendly gets you more to work with. No matter which tool you choose, scheduling a group with out the email threads feels amazing.

Calendly is ready when you are, and you can try it for free today at calendly dot com.

What happens at the end of my trial?

acceptedAnswer.text: At the end of your 14-day trial, you'll automatically be downgraded to the Free tier and you’ll be able to continue to use Calendly as long as you’d like. If you decide to upgrade to a paid plan, you can do so from the billing page in your account at any time during or after your trial.

mainEntity.name: Which plan is best for me and my team?

acceptedAnswer.text: Choose based on how much work around your meetings you want Calendly to handle. Standard and Teams focus on automating scheduling. Standard Plus and Teams Plus add Notetaker for meeting recaps, action items, and follow-up support, and Callie for email scheduling coordination and meeting prep and recall in Calendly. Enterprise adds admin, security, and scale for larger organizations, with tailored AI capabilities.

mainEntity.name: Can we try Calendly with multiple users?

acceptedAnswer.text: Absolutely! You can invite team members to join your trial account at no cost. At the end of your 14-day trial, all members will be automatically downgraded to the Free plan.

mainEntity.name: What does the renewal process look like?

acceptedAnswer.text: Paid subscriptions automatically renew for the same subscription period unless you downgrade your plan before your renewal date.

mainEntity.name: How do I upgrade or downgrade?

acceptedAnswer.text: Visit your billing page by going to My Account > Billing. From there, you can change your plan, add or remove user seats, and update your payment information.

mainEntity.name: We’re a non-profit organization, is there special pricing available?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, we offer special pricing to qualified non-profit organizations. Contact our customer support specialists for details: support@calendly.com

mainEntity.name: What payment methods do you accept?

acceptedAnswer.text: We accept Visa, Mastercard, American Express, Discover, JCB, and Diners Club credit and debit cards. Payment via PayPal is accepted for customers located outside the United States. Payment via invoice is available on the Standard or Teams plan for $5,000 and Enterprise plan for $15,000.
